_README: Drill-engine parity vectors: a target passage + the committed-character stream a signer produces -> the per-step (matched, index, complete) the drill engine decides. The drill engine (Epic 6a, #69) is strictly DOWNSTREAM of the committer, so -- unlike test_vectors.json / temporal_vectors.json -- these carry NO keypoints and NO timing, only emitted characters. Both platform ports run a DrillSession over each sequence and MUST produce identical per-step results. Assert the PER-STEP fields (they pin WHERE each advance lands, catching an off-by-one or a miss-advances-anyway port whose final index still matches); expected_final_* is the convenience rollup.
_generated_by: shared/tools/gen_drill_vectors.py (uv run). Generated, not hand-edited: the generator runs the reference DrillSession over every sequence and asserts the AUTHORED final (index, complete) before writing -- catching a mis-authored op stream. The per-step fields are recorded from the reference and are the cross-platform pins the parity harness enforces on each port (a port that diverges on any step fails even if its final state matches). Re-run after any change to the drill contract (shared/drill_contract.json).
_drill_contract: Per shared/drill_contract.json + ADR 0007: the engine consumes an already-validated target sequence (the source, 6a-3, sanitises a passage to the frozen ASCII alphabet A-Z / 0-9 / SPACE). It observes only NON-EMPTY committer emits. Match: ASCII-uppercase both the emit and the current target; hit iff equal. Under stay-until-success (iv-a, the only 6a-1 lifecycle) a hit advances the target index by one and a miss is a no-op; reaching the target count is COMPLETE (celebrate), after which further emits no-op. Later modes (timed iv-b, delayed-assist iv-d; 6a-6) add non-emit timeout transitions over this same target/index core and do not change the match rule.

_format.sequence_vectors: Each is {name, targets, steps:[...], expected_final_index, expected_final_complete}. Steps are observed in order; expected_final_* is the session state after the last step.
_format.targets: The drill's target sequence as a plain string; the engine splits it into single-character targets in order (frozen ASCII alphabet: A-Z / 0-9 / SPACE). Already validated -- the source (6a-3), not the engine, sanitises a passage into this.
_format.steps: Each step is EITHER an emit step {emit, expected_matched, expected_index, expected_complete} -- feed `emit` (one non-empty committed character) to session.observe and assert (matched, index, complete) -- OR a reset step {reset:true, expected_index, expected_complete}, where the harness calls session.reset() instead of observe() and asserts the index/complete afterwards (mirrors the reset frames in temporal_vectors.json).
_format.reset: Present and true only on a reset step; the harness calls session.reset().
_format.emit: One non-empty character as returned by the committer (absent on reset steps). Empty committer returns (mode switches, no-commit frames) are never observed by the drill, so they do not appear here.
_format.expected_matched: True iff normalized(emit) == normalized(current target); absent on reset steps.
_format.expected_index: The current target index AFTER this step (advances by one on a hit; unchanged on a miss).
_format.expected_complete: True once the index has reached the target count (the celebrate signal).
_format.expected_final_index: The session's index after the last step (rollup of the per-step expected_index).
_format.expected_final_complete: Whether the session is complete after the last step (rollup).
_format.name: Human-readable label for debugging. Ignored by the parity harness.
_format._note: Optional human explanation. Ignored by the parity harness.

sequence_vectors.name: clean_run_hello
sequence_vectors._note: Every committed letter matches the next target; the session advances five times and completes. The baseline happy path.

sequence_vectors.name: wrong_letter_stays_until_success
sequence_vectors._note: C misses target A (index stays 0); A hits (->1); Z misses target B (stays 1); B hits (->2, complete). Wrong letters never advance and are never penalised -- the defining stay-until-success behaviour.

sequence_vectors.name: case_insensitive_match
sequence_vectors._note: Lowercase targets, uppercase committer emits: both sides are ASCII-uppercased before comparison, so 'h'==('H') and 'i'==('I'). Pins the normalization rule identically across Python / Swift / Kotlin.

sequence_vectors.name: space_is_a_target
sequence_vectors._note: Targets split to ['A', ' ', 'B']; the committed space ' ' matches the space target. SPACE is a first-class character in a drill passage, not a separator the engine skips.

sequence_vectors.name: digit_target
sequence_vectors._note: To sign a digit the signer enters numeric mode, but those control-pose commits emit '' and are invisible to the drill. The drill sees only the committed '7', which matches the digit target.

sequence_vectors.name: double_letter_target
sequence_vectors._note: Two committed L's advance through two L targets. The committer's double-letter separator (brief REST, ADR 0005) is what yields two L commits; the drill is agnostic to how they were produced.

sequence_vectors.name: emits_after_complete_are_noops
sequence_vectors._note: A hits and completes the one-target session (->1). The trailing B is a no-op: matched False, index stays 1, complete stays True. The engine never advances past its target count.

sequence_vectors.name: wrong_letter_never_completes
sequence_vectors._note: Neither B nor C matches target A, so the index never advances and the session never completes. Stay-until-success means progress requires the correct sign.

sequence_vectors.name: mixed_letters_space_digit
sequence_vectors._note: Targets ['G', 'O', ' ', '2']; the committed letters, space, and digit each advance one target in order -> complete. Exercises all three frozen-alphabet character kinds in a single drill.

sequence_vectors.name: reset_replays_from_start
sequence_vectors._note: A, B advance to index 2; reset() returns the index to 0 (not complete); then A, B, C run cleanly to completion. Pins caller-driven reset across platforms (the committer vectors likewise exercise reset).

sequence_vectors.name: empty_targets_autocompletes
sequence_vectors._note: DrillSession('') has zero targets, so 0 >= 0 makes it COMPLETE from the start with no steps. A degenerate input the source (6a-3) must avoid; pinned only so the platforms agree on it.
